MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 19, 2018

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Romanelli, Giglia, Persichina, Pope

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal, Wroan, Retz*

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director

  STUDENTS PRESENT:  E. Hasama, S. Hasama

  * arrived later during the meeting

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 20, 2018

  COMMISSIONER POPE moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA

  TO APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY
  20, 2018

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  STREET TREES REMOVAL REQUEST

  Community Services Director Clark summarized the staff report, a request from the owner of
  property address, 9 Aurora Drive, to remove two City street trees and replace them with two trees
  planted in a location determined by the city.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission approve the removal of two Eucalyptus street trees located on each side of the
  driveway at #9 Aurora Drive and the purchase of two 15-gallon trees to be planted in a location(s)
  determined by the City at the cost of the applicant.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  1
COMMISSION MINUTES
MARCH 19, 2018
   VICE CHAIR GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE STAFFS RECOMMENDATION FOR THE REMOVAL OF TWO EUCALYPTUS
  STREET TREES LOCATED ON EACH SIDE OF THE DRIVEWAY AT #9 AURORA
  DRIVE AND THE PURCHASE OF TWO 15-GALLON TREES TO BE PLANTED IN A
  LOCATION(S) DETERMINED BY THE CITY AT THE COST OF THE APPLICANT.

  There being no objection, VICE ROMANELLI so moved.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  SUMMER MOVIE NIGHTS PROGRAM FILM SELECTION

  Community Services Director Clark stated that as directed by the Park and Activities Commission,
  staff has selected either, The Princess Bride or The Lion King as additional Summer Movie Night
  options.

  STUDENT E. HASAMA stated that The Lion King is a good choice. COMMISSIONER POPE
  agreed stating that considering the age group of the previous attendees, this is a good selection.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA to,

  APPROVE LION KING AS THE FINAL MOVIE SECTION FOR THE CITY’S SUMMER
  MOVIE NIGHT PROGRAM AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  B.  PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE

  Community Services Director Clark provided the Park and Activities Commission with the proposed
  park tours schedule.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Students E. Hasama and S. Hasama, are welcome
  to the Park and Activities Commission Meeting and Park Tour on May 21, 2018 at George F
  Canyon Park Nature Center.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the pocket park tour should be moved to a later date in the
  summer. Community Services Director Clark stated that by May 21st there should be a conceptual
  design of the park.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to,

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  C.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW

  Community Services Director provided a summary of the staff report and stated that staff met to
  discuss the various fee changes.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  2
COMMISSION MINUTES
MARCH 19, 2018
   Community Services Director stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities Commission
  make a recommendation to the City Council to increase the City’s recreation fees as recommended
  by staff and if recommended by the Race Subcommittee.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked if the barn stables are included in the fee structure. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that the deposit for the barn stables is $200 and it is charged if the
  barn stalls are not cleaned after use.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that there are still chairs at the barn stables that have been left from
  prior events and one of the regular equestrians’ has complained that she has had to clean-up the
  arena since the prior users do not. Community Services Director Clark stated that he has noted this
  and will look into it.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ arrived at 7:13 p.m.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the USTA Tennis Club and the Barn Stall fees have not been
  documented into the fee structure. Community Services Director Clark stated that people are buying
  more of the full USTA membership fee and stated that he will follow-up with having the fees included
  in the fee structure.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI commented that staff should be in a position to anticipate questions from the
  public regarding the increase in fees. Community Services Director Clark stated that most fees are
  supplemented, for example the sports field fees, to cover the cost.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE THE RECREATION FEES STRUCTURE AS PRESENTED.

  AYES: ROMANELLI, GIGLIA, RETZ, PERSICHINA, POPE
  NAYES:
  ABSENT: PORTUGAL, WROAN
  ABSTAIN:

  D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM

  Community Services Director Clark summarized the staff report and stated that the Equestrian
  Committee met in February to discuss the City Celebration event and concluded that they would
  like to move the equestrian events back to the Empty Saddle Club. Community Services Director
  Clark stated that the City Council was informed of this at the Policy Development meeting and there
  were no objections.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI asked if there was any discussion at the Equestrian Committee meeting
  regarding the impacts to the Betty’s Foundation partnership. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that the City Celebration in partnership with Betty’s Foundation will remain at Ernie Howlett
  Park.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked about the food service if the decision is made to go back to the Empty
  Saddle Club. Community Services Director Clark stated that the food would be provided by the 4H
  Club.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  3
COMMISSION MINUTES
MARCH 19, 2018
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that this item should go back to the City Celebration
  Subcommittee for discussion. VICE CHAIR GIGLIA agreed.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that one concern is that the equestrians are closer to the
  Empty Saddle Club and it creates for a longer day for them to bring horses and trailers to Ernie
  Howlett Park.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that consideration should be given to hold the entire event at the
  Empty Saddle Club and believes it is too early to dismiss the relationship with the equestrians and
  the city celebration event since there are changes that could be made to draw people and improve
  the event, but would also want to make sure that attention is given to the equestrians’ concerns.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA stated that it would be helpful to have an emcee announcing the various
  events going on during the festival. Community Services Director Clark indicated that Betty’s
  Foundation has been working towards getting Country Western/Folk musicians in order to tailor the
  event to the character of the city.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that the Equestrian Committee feels that they are losing
  attendance at the City Celebration event and feel that the Empty Saddle Club is a better venue.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that having the entire event at the Empty Saddle Club would likely not
  work due to the logistics of parking.

  The Park and Activities Commission agreed to hold the City Celebration Subcommittee meeting on
  Wednesday, April 11, 2018 at 7:00 p.m.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to:

  TABLE THIS ITEM AND BRING THIS ITEM TO BE DISCUSSED AT THE NEXT CITY
  CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING WITH THE PARTICIPATION OF
  REPRESENTATIVE(S) FROM THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE, CITY COUNCIL,
  BETTY’S FOUNDATION, AND THE EMPTY SADDLE CLUB.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORT

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that on Palos Verdes Drive East just before it turns into Narbonne
  Ave. on the opposite side of the street from the golf club entrance, there are multiple parts of the
  fence that need repair.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that at the dressage rink at Ernie Howlett Park there are several 3-rail
  fence standards that have split.

  B.  RACE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

  COMMISSIONER POPE provided a brief update on the meeting and stated that there is concern
  with the races that are scheduled prior to the city’s race, but stated that she does not feel that the
  city’s race will be impacted by the other races. However, the number of participants this year

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  4
COMMISSION MINUTES
MARCH 19, 2018
   should be reviewed in case there is a negative impact to the city’s race, but would like the city to
  continue to provide an opportunity for other non-profit organizations to be active in the community.
  She recommended that “How did you hear about the race”, be added to the race registration form.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DIRECTOR stated that he would like to add a question to the registration
  form of how many years the registrant has participated in the city’s race.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  FORM 700’s DUE – APRIL 2ND

  Community Services Director Clark reminded the Park and Activities Commissioners that forms
  are due.

  B.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST POCKET PARK DESIGN UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated Willdan has completed a survey of the pocket park at
  Palos Verdes Drive East at Harbor Sight. Due to the slope of the site, Willdan asked if the park
  would need to be ADA compliant. The question has been submitted to Joint Powers Insurance
  Authority and staff is awaiting a response.

  C.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated the City Council would like to come up with a parks or
  recreation facilities naming policy. The City Council would like the facilities to be named after
  persons who have made significant contributions to the city.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI asked if this would fall under Community Service Director Clarks’ purview.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that the city’s intern is working on researching the
  policies already in place in various cities.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ROMANELLI, Community Services Director Clark stated that
  there are several potential parks and facilities that need a name. The policy will be coming up for
  review by the Park and Activities Commission.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that a City Council Member expressed the need for a
  dog park in the city. He stated that back in 2009 this was reviewed by the Park and Activities
  Commission, there was a letter sent to Supervisor Knabe’s office suggesting the use of the Palos
  Verdes Landfill, which is maintained by Los Angeles County to create an enclosed dog park
  somewhere on the site. There is a letter prepared to Supervisor Hahn’s office and will be going
  out this week.

  A proposal from the representatives of the Romanian Festival to be a sister city. There are
  surrounding cities who have more than one sister city. There was no interest by the City Council.

  D.  PARK CONSULTANT SELECTION UPDATED

  Community Services Director Clark stated that a request for qualifications was sent out and there
  was only one consultant who responded. The City Manager has suggested to meet with the firm.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that Commissioner’s Pope and Retz are part of the Park
  Consultant Selection Subcommittee and he will provide dates and times for the interview.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  5
COMMISSION MINUTES
MARCH 19, 2018
   10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 27, 2018
  B.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 5, 2018
  C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 26, 2018

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager will
  have the Area G Coordinator come to a meeting to describe the various roles that the commission
  could assume in case of a citywide disaster.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that this came up at a Neighborhood Watch meeting and stated he
  would like this to go continue to move forward due to the importance of preparing for an emergency.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that at the next Equestrian Committee meeting, a horse
  census will be discussed and also who have trailers in order to plan for the transportation of moving
  horses during an emergency.

  B.  PARK AND FACILITY NAMING POLICY

  (Discussed earlier, see Item 9-C)

  12  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHNA made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA to,

  ADJOURN THE PARK AND ACTIVIIES MEETING AT 7:47 P.M.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  The next Park and Activities Meeting will be held on Monday, April 16, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, California.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea  Andy Clark
  Administrative Assistant  Community Services Director

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  6
